title: Unit Cost Orchestrator: rule-driven cost model and dry-run CLI
author: Maya Singh
description: Introduce a lightweight 'Unit Cost Orchestrator' that formalizes tenant-level unit-economics decisions into a rule-driven policy layer and a dry-run CLI for safe rollout. Motivation: teams need predictable, auditable cost defaults (batching, prefill/caching, and quant profiles) surfaced as a reusable policy that can be simulated before applying. This change implements: 1) a rules DSL and evaluation engine that maps workload signatures to cost-aware defaults (batch target, cache TTL, quant profile tiers); 2) an 'econctl' CLI with 'simulate' and 'apply' subcommands for dry-run and canary rollout; 3) new telemetry (inference.unit_cost_estimate, econ.rule_evaluations, prefill.prefetch_ratio) and tracing hooks for debugging policy decisions; 4) a small in-memory policy store plus optional persistence to the existing config DB; 5) safety gates for automatic fallback to conservative quant profiles under error or when latency SLOs are breached. Checklist: - [x] Rules DSL syntax and parser - [x] Orchestrator evaluation loop + caching of rule results - [x] econctl CLI with --dry-run and --canary flags - [x] Unit tests covering rule corner cases and fallback paths - [x] Integration test that exercises metrics emitted by a simulated tenant - [x] Documentation page and example policy bundle - [x] E2E smoke in CI with feature-flag enabled Related: ENG-4567 (policy workstream), SUP-2128 (customer request for safe defaults).
commits: init: add rules DSL and parser; feat: implement orchestrator evaluation loop and cache; feat(cli): add econctl simulate/apply; perf: memoize rule evaluations; telemetry: emit unit_cost_estimate and rule_evaluations; test: add unit and integration tests; docs: add policy guide and examples
review_thread: Jonah: Can the DSL express conditional quant fallbacks based on latency percentiles? Author: Yes, added 'latency_percentile' predicate and tests. Sofia: Suggest splitting policy store persistence behind a feature flag — good for rollout. Author: Added ci/feature-flags.yml and default OFF. Eli: CI flaked on integration test first run (timeout), rerun succeeded; left a minor suggestion to tighten metric names. Author: Addressed metric names and added more defensive parsing for malformed policies.
release_notes: Add Unit Cost Orchestrator: rule-based defaults for batching, cache TTL, and quant profiles; new econctl CLI for dry-run simulation and safe apply; emits inference.unit_cost_estimate and econ.rule_evaluations metrics. Feature gated behind 'econ_orchestrator' flag.
risk_assessment: low-medium: new policy layer is feature-flagged with conservative defaults and automatic fallbacks to existing quant profiles; added telemetry for quick rollbacks.
rollout_strategy: Enable feature-flag OFF by default. Steps: 1) smoke canary with internal tenant (2% traffic) using econctl --canary; 2) monitor inference.unit_cost_estimate and latency SLOs for 48h; 3) if stable, progressively increase traffic over 24-72h; 4) immediate auto-fallback if rule evaluation fails or latency breach detected.
release_window: recommended low-traffic window (weekend nights) and post-deployment monitoring for 48 hours
